lesson.subject: general-knowledge
lesson.title: Weather and the Seasons
lesson.summary: Name the weather, measure it and see how the year turns through four seasons.
learning_objectives: Say why we have seasons in simple words

standards.text: Identify seasonal and daily weather patterns in the United Kingdom and the location of hot and cold areas of the world

success_criteria: I can use a thermometer and a rain gauge
I can order the four seasons
lesson.real_life: Monsoon rain in Lahore, snow in Murree, long summer evenings and drizzle in the UK, and Eid in different seasons.

warm_up.prompt: What do we use an umbrella for?

options.text: To keep dry in the rain

warm_up.hint: It is part of the year.

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: how does the weather change through the year?
blocks.say: Today we ask a big question. What is the weather like today?

blocks.alt: Many small rain drops on a window with a dark blue and green background
blocks.caption: Raindrops on a window. Rain is one kind of weather.
blocks.credit: Photo by ERIC ZHU on Unsplash
blocks.say: Rain drops cling to this window. Rain is one kind of weather.

blocks.text: Stop 1: Sunny, rainy, windy and snowy

blocks.markdown: **Weather** is what the air and sky are like today.
blocks.say: Weather is what the air outside is like today. It can change in a day.

scenes.caption: Sunny.
scenes.say: It is sunny. The sky is blue and the Sun is bright.

scenes.caption: Rainy.
scenes.say: It is rainy. Water falls from grey clouds.

scenes.caption: Windy.
scenes.say: It is windy. Moving air blows the kites and trees.

scenes.caption: Snowy.
scenes.say: It is snowy. Snow falls in cold places like Murree.

question.prompt: Which weather has water falling from the clouds?
question.explanation: Rain is water falling from clouds.

blocks.markdown: A **symbol** is a little picture that stands for something.
blocks.say: On the news, weather has little pictures called symbols. A sun means sunny.

scenes.caption: Sun.
scenes.say: A sun is the symbol for a sunny day.

scenes.caption: Rain.
scenes.say: A cloud with drops is the symbol for rain.

scenes.caption: Snow.
scenes.say: A snowflake is the symbol for snow.

question.prompt: A snowflake is the symbol for a sunny day.
question.explanation: A snowflake means snow, not sun.

blocks.title: Zainab's weather diary
blocks.transcript: Zainab starts a weather diary in Lahore. On Monday it is sunny and very hot. On Wednesday the sky fills with grey clouds. On Thursday the wind blows her kite. On Friday the monsoon rain arrives. The rain gauge fills up. She measures the rain. She puts all the days in a weather table. Summer in Lahore has the monsoon. Weather follows the seasons.
blocks.caption: Zainab keeps a weather diary for a week in Lahore and sees the monsoon arrive.

points: Weather is what the air is like today
blocks.say: Let us remember. Weather can be sunny, rainy, windy or snowy. We use symbols for it.

terms.meaning: What the air and sky are like today.
A little picture that stands for something.
Bright with the Sun shining.
With rain falling.
With a lot of moving air.
With snow falling.

blocks.say: We can measure weather. A thermometer tells us how hot or cold it is.

blocks.markdown: **Temperature** tells us how hot or cold something is.
blocks.say: Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius. We write it as °C.

scenes.caption: Thermometer.
scenes.say: A thermometer shows temperature. A high number means hot.

scenes.caption: Rain gauge.
scenes.say: A rain gauge is a tube. It collects rain so we can measure it.

scenes.caption: Wind vane.
scenes.say: A wind vane points the way the wind is blowing.

question.prompt: Which tool measures how hot or cold it is?

blocks.markdown: A **table** lists facts in rows and columns.
blocks.say: A table helps us keep our weather facts in order. Each day gets a row.

scenes.caption: Monday.
scenes.say: On Monday it is sunny and 30 degrees.

scenes.caption: Tuesday.
scenes.say: On Tuesday it is rainy and 24 degrees.

scenes.caption: Compare.
scenes.say: A table makes it easy to compare the days.

blocks.title: Wet or dry?
blocks.goal: Move each weather word. Rain goes in Wet. Sunshine goes in Dry.
blocks.say: Sort the weather. Does each one belong with Wet or Dry?

blocks.title: Make a weather table
instructions: Draw a table with a row for each day.
Look out of the window each day.
Write the weather in the row.

question.prompt: A table helps us compare the weather on different days.

blocks.say: Let us remember. We measure weather with tools. A table keeps our facts tidy.

terms.meaning: A tool that measures temperature.
How hot or cold something is.
A tube that collects rain to measure it.
A tool that shows which way the wind blows.
Facts set out in rows and columns.
The scale we use to measure temperature.

mini_quiz.prompt: What does a rain gauge collect?
A wind vane shows which way the wind is blowing.
mini_quiz.explanation: A wind vane shows wind direction.

blocks.text: Stop 1: Clothes and fruit for each season

blocks.markdown: A **season** is a part of the year with its own weather.
blocks.say: A year has four seasons: spring, summer, autumn and winter. They come round again and again.

scenes.caption: Spring.
scenes.say: Spring is mild. New leaves and flowers come out.

scenes.caption: Summer.
scenes.say: Summer is hot. We wear light clothes and eat mangoes.

scenes.caption: Autumn.
scenes.say: Autumn is cooler. Leaves turn brown and fall.

scenes.caption: Winter.
scenes.say: Winter is cold. We wear a coat, a scarf and a hat.

blocks.alt: A path covered in red and orange leaves under trees with orange autumn leaves
blocks.caption: Autumn leaves on a path. Leaves change colour as the weather turns cooler.
blocks.credit: Photo by Konstantin Dyadyun on Unsplash
blocks.say: The seasons go round like a wheel. After winter comes spring again.

blocks.markdown: The Earth's **tilt** gives us the seasons.
blocks.say: The Earth goes round the Sun once a year. Its tilt gives us seasons.

blocks.title: Seasons wheel
blocks.goal: Watch the order, then copy it. It gets longer each time!
blocks.say: Warm up your memory. Watch the season pictures light up, then copy them.

points: The Earth's tilt gives us seasons
blocks.say: Let us remember. There are four seasons. They come round again every year.

mini_quiz.prompt: How many seasons are in a year?

blocks.markdown: A **diary** is a record you write each day.
blocks.say: A weather diary shows weather over a week. We draw a symbol for each day.

scenes.caption: A diary.
scenes.say: Write the day. Draw the symbol. Add the temperature.

scenes.caption: Seven days.
scenes.say: Do this every day for a week.

scenes.caption: Count.
scenes.say: At the end, count the symbols. Which weather happened most?

question.prompt: What do we draw each day in a weather diary?

blocks.text: Stop 2: Compare Pakistan and the UK

blocks.markdown: The **monsoon** is a season of heavy rain.
blocks.say: In Lahore the monsoon rain arrives in summer. It can pour for hours.

blocks.alt: A white bicycle covered in snow beside houses with snowy roofs at sunrise
blocks.caption: Snow on a bicycle in a cold country. Winter weather is very different from Lahore's summer.
blocks.say: In the UK, it often drizzles in any season. Summer evenings are long.

scenes.caption: Lahore.
scenes.say: Lahore has a hot summer and the monsoon.

scenes.caption: Murree.
scenes.say: Murree has cold snowy winters.

scenes.caption: The UK.
scenes.say: The UK is often cool and rainy, with a few warm days.
